problem.display_name: Lab: Three Rounds on One Draft

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Your revision fixed the missing total but reintroduced an error you had already corrected. What is the right next move?

choice.div: Stop iterating; take the best draft and edit it yourself, keeping a record of what is fixed.
Ask for another full rewrite with "be more careful".
Accept the draft because the total is now right.

div.p: Regression is the signal that the loop has stopped converging. Human editing is the cheaper, safer finish.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which critique is most useful to give the model?

choice.div: "The risk section names no owner; add one named role and keep the rest unchanged."

div.p: Specific, bounded, and scoped to one change. Unbounded feedback invites a rewrite of what already worked.

choice.div: So you can see which instruction actually caused the improvement and avoid repeating failures.
Because the tool requires a log to run.
To prove the model was used.

div.p: The log converts trial and error into a method you can reuse on the next task.

choiceresponse.p: Which are signs that further iteration is not helping? Select all that apply.

choice.div: The output grows longer without new information.
You cannot state what "more natural" would mean.
You have stopped checking facts and are only wordsmithing.
The draft is shorter than the previous one.

div.p: Drift, regressions, vague goals and abandoned verification mean the loop is done. Length alone says nothing.
